messages:
matt: FYI observed a canary gone sideways this morning — 30% of traffic landed on the OLD model even though console rollout shows 80/20 new/old. Noticed a feature-flag check in the runtime that seems to re-route some users. Anyone know which config should win when both exist?
jia: Can you paste the runtime log + the rollout YAML? Might be an ordering issue.
matt: log excerpt: `route: new_model` then later `feature_flag_check: false -> routed to old_model` — so runtime applied flag after policy. rollout YAML from console: ```rollout:
  id: r-2026-03-canary
  split:
    - variant: new_model
      pct: 80
    - variant: old_model
      pct: 20
  guards:
    - name: max-latency
      enabled: true
```
ops-bot: Routing event summary (06:42): 1200 reqs total, 360 routed to old_model, 840 to new_model. 310 of the old_model hits were matched by a runtime flag check for `matt-experiment`.
kevin: This is the classic "concurrent split" problem. Currently the runtime has a short-circuit flag check used by some SDKs for fast toggles; console rollouts are evaluated by the policy engine. There's no documented merge strategy, so teams end up composing both and surprising traffic distribution.
anika: Is the runtime short-circuit intentional? I thought console rollouts should be the canonical split for traffic experiments.
kevin: Historically we implemented flag short-circuit to allow SREs/product to kill a feature quickly without touching the policy engine. That was never reconciled with the rollout layer.
liz-product: From product POV, we want predictable experiments: console split = the experiment. Feature flags are fine for kill-switches but they should be explicit "override" and visible in the rollout UI.
matt: Agreed. Current UX: console shows 80% new which makes PMs assume 80% reach, but the runtime flag hidden in codelet flips a subset back to old. Very confusing for experiments/metrics.
jia: Proposal: define explicit precedence and small compatibility rules:
- 1) If a flag is named with prefix `override/` treat it as emergency override and document it. Emit a dashboard banner when such flags exist.
- 2) By default, policy rollouts determine split. Runtime flags must opt-in to influence traffic split for an experiment.
- 3) If both apply and conflict, log a conflict telemetry event and increment a counter + show warning in rollout UI.
kevin: Implementation notes: we can add a validation check in the policy ingestion API to detect conflicting flags (heuristic: flags referenced by code matching rollout id or matched user cohort). Also add a precedence field to the rollout API: `split_precedence: policy|flags|merge` so teams can opt behavior.
anika: Careful: adding `split_precedence` gives teams more knobs which increases complexity. Prefer a single sane default (policy wins) with explicit `override` semantics.
liz-product: Agreed default = policy wins; override flags must be created via console or marked in the flag service with `emergency:true` so they appear in the experiment timeline.
matt: Short-term mitigation: (1) migrate the SRE short-circuit to a dedicated emergency override flag that sets `emergency:true` in flag service; (2) add a rollout UI banner that checks for active emergency flags impacting the rollout and shows the realtime estimate of effective split.
jia: I'll put up a PR for telemetry: emit `rollout_conflict_detected` event with payload keys: rollout_id, flag_keys, affected_pct. That will let analytics alert on discrepant metrics.
kevin: Backend changes: policy evaluator should accept an optional flag precedence override in the request context; default behavior: policy evaluation result returned and SDK should not re-route unless flag is emergency. We'll also add a server-side check that fails build-time if a runtime flag with `emergency:true` isn't registered in console (safety guard).
anika: UX asks: show a clear “effective split” in the rollout preview that accounts for known overrides. This should be near-term and low-effort.
liz-product: I'll prioritize the UI banner and docs update. Also want a short blurb in GA notes about "how flags and rollouts interact".
matt: Thanks — can someone own the spec? I can take the API + runtime regression tests if kevin can own the evaluator change and jia the telemetry/UI bits.
kevin: I can own evaluator change + server validation.
jia: I'll file the PRs for telemetry and the rollout UI banner.
anika: I'll draft the docs for the new default semantics and emergency-flag pattern.
liz-product: I'll coordinate with PMs and SRE to migrate active emergency short-circuits this week. :+1:
matt: Cool. One more ask: add an admin-only endpoint that simulates effective routing for a given user bucket so PMs can preview real reach (takes into account emergency flags). That would have prevented this incident.
kevin: Good idea. Added to the implementation TODOs.
ops-bot: Action items created: #ENG-PLAT-942 (spec + API), #ENG-PLAT-943 (evaluator + validation), #ENG-PLAT-944 (telemetry + UI banner), #ENG-PLAT-945 (docs & migration).
matt: Thanks everyone, will follow up after PRs land.
